performed_via_github_app.description:
Codecov provides highly integrated tools to group, merge, archive and compare coverage reports. Whether your team is comparing changes in a pull request or reviewing a single commit, Codecov will improve the code review workflow and quality.

## Code coverage done right.®

1. Upload coverage reports from your CI builds.
2. Codecov merges all builds and languages into one beautiful coherent report.
3. Get commit statuses, pull request comments and coverage overlay via our browser extension.

When Codecov merges your uploads it keeps track of the CI provider (inc. build details) and user specified context, e.g. `#unittest` ~ `#smoketest` or `#oldcode` ~ `#newcode`. You can track the `#unittest` coverage independently of other groups. [Learn more here](
http://docs.codecov.io/docs/flags)

Through **Codecov's Browser Extension** reports overlay directly in GitHub UI to assist in code review in [Chrome](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/codecov/gedikamndpbemklijjkncpnolildpbgo) or Firefox (https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/codecov/)

*Highly detailed* **pull request comments** and *customizable* **commit statuses** will improve your team's workflow and code coverage incrementally.

**File backed configuration** all through the `codecov.yml`. 

## FAQ
- Do you **merge multiple uploads** to the same commit? **Yes**
- Do you **support multiple languages** in the same project? **Yes**
- Can you **group coverage reports** by project and/or test type? **Yes**
- How does **pricing** work? Only paid users can view reports and post statuses/comments.

body:
This issue also impacts us.
could you please expedite ?

While working on batching performance I noticed something in `pdata/internal/state.go` that I can't tell is intentional. I didn't want to file a bug report in case it's a deliberate tradeoff.

`State` holds two fields with different concurrency treatment:

```go
type State struct {
	refs  atomic.Int32
	state uint32
}
```

`refs` is atomic. `state` is not. `MarkReadOnly` does `st.state |= stateReadOnlyBit`, and `MarkPipelineOwned` does a check-then-act:

```go
func (st *State) MarkPipelineOwned() bool {
	if st.state&statePipelineOwnedBit != 0 {
		return false
	}
	st.state |= statePipelineOwnedBit
	return true
}
```

`IsReadOnly`, `AssertMutable`, and `MarkPipelineOwned` also read `st.state` with no synchronisation. By the Go memory model that looks like a data race, and the check-then-act in particular could let two goroutines both return `true`.

What made me look twice is that `MarkReadOnly` is called per request from `internal/fanoutconsumer` for all four signals, on the shared path every request goes through. `MarkPipelineOwned` is narrower, reached via `service/internal/refconsumer`. I also noticed that `state_test.go` covers one method out of eight, and none of them concurrently.

I couldn't run the race detector to confirm. `go test -race` fails to start on my machine with `exit status 0xc0000139`, and it does the same on a trivial test in an empty module, so I don't think it's specific to this code. This is a reading of the source, not an observed failure.

Two things I'd like your view on before I go further:

1. **Is the current encoding deliberate?** Making `state` an `atomic.Uint32` would put an atomic operation on `MarkReadOnly` and on every `AssertMutable`, and `AssertMutable` runs on every mutating setter in pdata. If the current form is a deliberate tradeoff, that settles it.

2. **If it is a race and you want it addressed, would a concurrent test be welcome?** A test that exercises these methods from multiple goroutines would run under upstream's race-enabled CI. It would either catch the problem or show it isn't reachable in practice, and both outcomes are useful.

Tangential to this PR, so I can move it to its own issue if you prefer.

> This issue also impacts us. could you please expedite ?

+1, many thanks for addressing this issue

## What is [CodSpeed](https://codspeed.io)?
CodSpeed is a **continuous benchmarking** platform that allows you to **track** and **compare** the **performance** of your codebase during development.

It uses a smart **runtime engine** to measure the performance of your code in an **accurate** and **reproducible** way without creating a huge **runtime overhead**, unlike traditional benchmarks.

CodSpeed produces detailed **performance reports** helping you **improve** your codebase **performance**, directly **within your repository provider** (Pull Requests comments, Merge checks, ...).

## How it works

The core of the **performance measurement** is done directly within your **CI environment** through the **CodSpeed Action**. Allowing you to **stay the sole owner** of your data and to keep your **codebase private**.

Once the performance data is generated, **only the benchmark results** are sent to the CodSpeed servers to be **analyzed**.

Then, performance reports are **generated** and **published** directly **within your repository provider**.

## How long does it take to install?

If you're **already benchmarking** your codebase, you can plug your **existing benchmarks** to CodSpeed in **less than 5 minutes** since CodSpeed benchmark's API is **compatible** with the most **popular benchmarking frameworks**.

If **you haven't any benchmarks yet**, we provide an **intuitive** benchmarking API that allows you to **create your first benchmarks** in a **few minutes**.
